evals.name: full-audit-before-build
evals.prompt: health check the docs before we start building — audit the whole project for gaps and contradictions
evals.setup: Before running, seed the project copy with two defects: (a) in one shaped spec's tasks.md, delete the task that covers its last AC; (b) in that epic's specs.index.yml, change the spec's status to a value that differs from its spec.md.
evals.expected_output: Read-only full-project audit in chat: top line with files checked, verdict and severity counts; high/med findings grouped by level with both sides quoted path:line, downstream impact and fix command; low as one-liners; checked-no-issues list by level; ends by asking which findings to fix. No files modified.
assertions: Top line states files checked, a verdict (CLEAN or ISSUES FOUND) and counts by severity
Findings are grouped by severity (high / med / low)
Every high and med finding quotes at least two path:line locations
Every finding names a fix (a slash command or 'manual edit')
Report includes a 'checked, no issues' list by level
Report ends by asking which findings to fix (and does not claim to have fixed anything)
No project file in the copy was modified (read-only)
Detects seeded defect (a): reports the AC with no covering task, quoting the spec.md line
Detects seeded defect (b): reports the status mismatch between specs.index.yml and spec.md
Covers root-level docs (any *.md at the repo root outside softwareos/) in what was checked

evals.name: epic-scoped-audit
evals.setup: Before running, seed the project copy with two defects: (a) in one accounts-auth spec.md, add a reference to a standards file that does not exist; (b) in a spec of a different epic, add the same defect (it must NOT be reported, since it is out of scope).
evals.expected_output: Audit scoped to the accounts-auth epic (its epic.md, tech-plan, brief, specs, specs.index.yml) checked against product docs and standards; cross-epic ownership collisions involving its specs; same report format; asks which to fix. No files modified.
assertions: Top line states files checked, a verdict (CLEAN or ISSUES FOUND) and counts by severity
Findings are grouped by severity (high / med / low)
Every high and med finding quotes at least two path:line locations
Every finding names a fix (a slash command or 'manual edit')
Report includes a 'checked, no issues' list by level
Report ends by asking which findings to fix (and does not claim to have fixed anything)
No project file in the copy was modified (read-only)
Stays scoped to accounts-auth: no findings that live only in other epics' files
Detects seeded defect (a): reports the broken standards reference in the accounts-auth spec with its path:line
Does not report seeded defect (b) in the other epic

evals.name: after-infra-plan-fallthrough
evals.prompt: we've been applying the stuff in INFRA_PLAN.md to the docs over the last few days. did anything fall through? is the softwareos folder still consistent with itself and with the root docs?
evals.setup: Before running, seed the project copy with one partially-cascaded decision: add a new env var (e.g. REDIS_URL) to INFRA_PLAN.md and to architecture.md, but not to dependencies.md or tech-stack.md.
evals.expected_output: Full audit that specifically checks INFRA_PLAN.md and design-rationale.md against product docs and specs, flags partially-cascaded decisions with /update-arch as fix, same report format, asks which to fix. No files modified.
assertions: Top line states files checked, a verdict (CLEAN or ISSUES FOUND) and counts by severity
Findings are grouped by severity (high / med / low)
Every high and med finding quotes at least two path:line locations
Every finding names a fix (a slash command or 'manual edit')
Report includes a 'checked, no issues' list by level
Report ends by asking which findings to fix (and does not claim to have fixed anything)
No project file in the copy was modified (read-only)
Explicitly checks INFRA_PLAN.md against softwareos docs and reports what was/wasn't cascaded
Detects the seeded partial cascade: the env var is in INFRA_PLAN.md/architecture.md but missing from dependencies.md or tech-stack.md, with /update-arch as the fix
